Action Plan:
1. Provide a labelled container and instructions for a mid-stream urine (MSU) sample today; perform on-site dipstick and send for microscopy, culture & sensitivities (MC&S). Contact patient with results when available.  
2. Issue prescription for a 3-day course of an oral antibiotic effective for uncomplicated cystitis (doctor offered trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin; final agent/dose not documented).  
3. Advise generous oral hydration and use paracetamol as required for pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
4. Safety-netting: patient to seek urgent review if fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or worsening symptoms develop; routine follow-up or review in 1 week if no improvement.  
5. Sexual health advice: discussed pregnancy risk (LMP 2 weeks ago) and STI risk with unprotected intercourse; advised condom use and offered Chlamydia/Gonorrhoea screening if symptoms persist or recur.  
6. Lifestyle counselling: discouraged further cannabis use; patient receptive.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging on urination, increased urinary frequency, and suprapubic aching pain, onset ≈6–7 days ago.  
• Hematuria: Pink-tinged urine noted today.  
• Denies flank/back pain, fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting.  
• Bowel habit unchanged from baseline IBS (variable stool consistency).  
• No abnormal vaginal discharge; sexually active with long-term boyfriend, unprotected intercourse 1–2 weeks ago.

- Combined oral contraceptive pill (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Social history: 19-year-old university student living in halls; occasional social alcohol; tried cannabis once 1.5 weeks ago; non-smoker.

• No physical examination performed (telephone consult). Patient afebrile by history.
